name: clover

purpose.why: Rebuilt on Evan's request (2026-10-22) to replace the Ranch tile's original model with a crafted one, keeping its game role.
purpose.audience: children building and playing in a miniature ranch
purpose.style: normal (upgrade: the same asset, built better)

brief.prompt: a low patch of pasture clover with round white and pink flower heads

concept.tool: Midjourney web app (midjourney.com/imagine), driven in Evan's signed-in Chrome by Claude through the Claude in Chrome extension, one job at a time, text prompts only (no image reference)

hero.prompt: a low patch of pasture clover with round white and pink flower heads, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 1:1
hero.pick_reason: low patch with readable trefoil leaves and round white-pink heads, whole patch with margin

construction.by: modeler agent, directed by the art director (Claude)

rounds.change: First build: 46 mound and 10 edge trefoils (30-38 mm leaflets) on a peaked dome, 30 bipyramid heads up to 0.205 m. Camera calibrated to yaw 0 / elev 22.
Bigger leaflets (38-48 mm), a wider, flatter-topped dome (pow 0.55), bigger, rounder heads, heads capped at 0.19 m.
Rounder leaflet outline and heads at 0.18 m. A deeper footprint (0.682) was reverted.
14 edge trefoils on a wider, shallower rim (0.40 x 0.32 m), heads capped at 0.17 m.
Head height set as a rise above the leaf dome (short buds on the face, tall in the middle), 32 heads, 44 mound trefoils, 6 grass blades, seed 23, softer cream.
Leaves layered higher (70-100 % of the dome), more outward tilt at the rim, lighter core and thinner grass. Final render at 768 px / 48 samples.

what_was_done: Per the art director, the hero is the only target (no turnaround). make_views.py keys the hero against its cream backdrop and drops the cast shadow on the right and the thin strips under the front leaves. The shadow is a desaturated grey-green (blue close to green) while the leaves are saturated, so below row 1080 every pixel with B/G above 0.74 is dropped, except two boxes around low pink heads. The result is views/hero_mask.png.

hero_check.py renders front-on from 22 deg up with the harness lens and scores against views/hero_mask.png. A yaw/elevation grid put the best at yaw 0 to 10 and elevation 20 to 25. I fixed it at 0/22 and held it there.

44 trefoils sit on an elliptical dome (0.36 x 0.28 m, 0.12 m high, profile (1-r^2)^0.55, so the top is flat and wide). Each one sits at 70 to 100 % of the dome height, so the leaves stack in layers. They tilt outward from about 9 deg in the middle to about 70 deg at the rim. 14 loose trefoils lie almost flat around a 0.40 x 0.32 m rim. A low 24-triangle dome (Leaf_Shade) under the leaves keeps the mound solid where the cards leave gaps, and reads as the hero's shaded depths between the leaves.

Three leaflets per leaf, each a 3-triangle fan (centre, two shoulders, two tips: a rounded, slightly heart-shaped card 38 to 48 mm long). The shoulders cup up and the tips droop. 35 % are Leaf_Pale and the rest Leaf_Green. The material is double-sided.

32 clover heads, each a 4-sided bipyramid (8 triangles, radius 12.5 to 15.5 mm). Each stands on a thin 3-sided Stem_Green stem that leans out from nearer the centre. A head rises 12 to 80 mm above the leaf dome, skewed short and taller in the middle, with a cap of 0.185 m. So the short pink buds sit on the mound's face and the tall cream heads stand in the middle. The heads are Petal_Cream with a Petal_Pink lower half (pink-tipped), fully cream, or fully pink, and the lowest ones are mostly pink.
6 thin single-triangle Leaf_Grass blades poke through at the front base.

1,000 triangles (ground plant budget 1k) in 7 meshes with one flat material each: Leaf_Green, Leaf_Pale, Leaf_Shade, Leaf_Grass, Stem_Green, Petal_Cream, Petal_Pink. All are double-sided and fall in the game's foliage role, so the seasons recolour them. Origin at the footprint centre on the ground, front -Y, no animation. Size 0.415 x 0.354 x 0.199 m against the old UP-051's 0.405 x 0.363 x 0.330 m.
construction.creative_additions: A dark low-poly core dome under the leaves stands in for the shaded depths of the patch. The lowest heads are mostly pink buds, as in the hero.

geometry.up: Z (Blender source); Y in GLB and game
geometry.origin: centre of the footprint, on the ground

good: Hero IoU 0.748 from the matched camera at the final 768 px / 48 samples render. The low, wide, flat-topped mound spilling into loose flat trefoils at the edges matches the hero's outline.
Bold blocks of colour that read at tile size: two leaf greens, dark gaps, and cream and pink heads standing above the mound.
Exactly at the 1k budget, with no need for 1.5k.
off: Height: the footprint is kept (0.415 x 0.354 m against the old 0.405 x 0.363 m), but the height drops from 0.33 to 0.20 m. The hero is a mound about half as tall as it is wide, and keeping both the old footprint and the old height would have made a tall clump, not the hero. The old model was three tall stalks.
The heads are 8-triangle bipyramids, so up close they read as faceted diamonds rather than the hero's fluffy florets. The pink lower half stands in for the hero's drooping pink outer florets.
The hero has fine grass and many small leaves deep in the mound. Here a few large trefoils over a dark core stand in for them, so the inner gaps read darker and blockier.
The IoU moves about ±0.02 with the random seed. The seed (23) was picked from a small set by score, so part of the last gain is luck in the edge layout.

rights: Original work for Abbie's World. Concept art generated on Evan's Midjourney account; geometry generated procedurally, no third-party meshes or textures.
